Presentation Element Atlas

An open catalog of slide elements: what each one is, when to use it, and a live demo of how it works. Search or filter, open a demo, and copy the idea into your own talk.

Navigation & deck chrome17

Persistent controls around the slides: wayfinding, pacing, presenter tools.

“More detail” drawer

Advanced

Side panel that opens per-slide backup notes without leaving the slide.

Best for Keeping slides clean while having depth ready for questions.

nav

Agenda / contents tracker

Small header showing the section list with the current section highlighted.

Best for Consulting-style decks with many sections.

nav

Chapter switcher menu

Top-bar dropdown that shows the current chapter and lists every chapter and slide for direct jumps.

Best for Long talks where the presenter or audience needs to jump between chapters.

nav

Clicks slider

Advanced

Presenter scrubber that steps through every build on a slide.

Best for Rehearsing complex builds.

nav

Context-aware Next / Reveal button

Advanced

Primary button that reads “Reveal” while a slide has builds left and “Next” when it is done.

Best for Talks with progressive builds, so the presenter never skips a step.

nav

Drawing & laser overlay

Freehand ink and a laser pointer drawn over the live slide.

Best for Pointing at details, workshops.

nav

In-deck search

Full-text search across slides.

Best for Reference decks and long decks.

nav

Overview / grid mode

Zoomed-out grid of all slides for jumping.

Best for Rehearsal, and jumping back during Q&A.

nav

Pacing timer

Advanced

Per-slide time budget that shows whether you are ahead of or behind schedule.

Best for Strict time slots and timed talks.

nav

Presenter panel (quiet button)

Advanced

Low-visibility button that opens presenter-only notes, ready for Q&A or any point in the talk.

Best for Keeping prompts for Q&A available without showing them to the audience.

nav

Remote control from phone

Advancing slides from a phone over a shared link.

Best for Presenting away from the laptop.

nav

Return-to-hub button

Advanced

Floating “Back to topics” control that appears after jumping from a hub slide.

Best for Non-linear Q&A navigation.

nav

Segmented progress bar

Row of dashes, one per slide, grouped by chapter, with the current position filled.

Best for Showing how far along the talk is and where chapters break.

nav

Skip link and slide announcer

Advanced

Keyboard skip link plus a screen-reader live region announcing “Slide N of M: title”.

Best for Accessible web decks.

nav

Sources panel

Global top-bar entry that opens the references and data sources behind the talk.

Best for Evidence-heavy talks such as research readouts and reviews.

nav

Speaker view

Second window with notes, a timer, a pacing clock and the next-slide preview.

Best for Live delivery.

nav

Vertical (2D) slide stacks

Advanced

Slides nested under a topic so that down means detail and right means next topic.

Best for Optional deep dives.

nav
